findings.rationale: GU (n=708, the smallest-but-one client) is the clear low outlier on update cosine: its mean cosine to the median update is 0.2145, the lowest of all 52 clients (typical clients 0.4-0.7), with min cos -0.15. Its median norm ratio (1.004) carries a size-adjusted flag of z=+4.0. Per-round values are erratic: norm ratios range 0.36 to 2.26 and cosines swing between -1 and +1 (e.g. -1 at rounds 6 and 16, -0.97 at round 18), which is the signature of large random noise in uploads rather than consistent local training. Supporting but weaker signals from other screens: a drift flag on Sex (max_shift_sd z=+3.3) and a Sex=1 subgroup O/E of 1.62 (z_noise 3.37). No single statistic exceeds |z|~6, and noise at this client size is large, so confidence is moderate. Budget was exhausted before attribution_churn could confirm the explanation jitter directly.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then used the remaining budget on narrower re-queries (MO, GU, CT, WI, GU/VI/AL drift, WV/GU/VI features). Most outliers were small-client noise: they did not persist across calls (e.g. CT AgeGroup 12 outcome rate 0.905 in the screen but 0.063 in the re-query; VI and WV feature percentiles changed sign between calls). Leads I did not report because they fall below the evidence bar: MO has a steady decline in update norm across rounds (median norm z=-4.2, min z=-4.5) with no independent confirmation; WI AgeGroup 5 shows observed outcome far above predicted in two calls (z about 3); WV and VI feature-tail anomalies are inconsistent between calls; GU's prevalence (0.205) exceeds its mean prediction (0.134) but its client-performance flags are empty. I report GU only, as a moderate-confidence finding (explanation_instability): its update cosines are the lowest in the federation and erratic across rounds. The federation is otherwise consistent with clean; attribution_churn was not run because the budget ran out.
